title: Experiences & comparisons
description: HSK 3: talk about what you've done (过, 是…的), compare Denmark and China (比, 跟…一样) and give reasons (因为…所以, 虽然…但是). Ends with a longer listening challenge.

words.note: After a verb: 去过 = have been to. Usually unstressed.
第一次 = the first time, 第二 = second.

exchanges.context: A relative checks how you're settling in.
At dinner they want your honest opinion.

grammar.title: 过 = have ever done
grammar.body: Verb + 过 talks about experience: 我去过北京 = I've been to Beijing. Negative: 我没去过 (never 不去过). Ask: 你去过…吗？

grammar.title: 是…的 for details of the past
grammar.body: When something already happened and you ask about when, how or where, wrap the detail in 是…的: 你是什么时候来的？ 我是坐飞机来的. In speech, 是 is often dropped, but 的 stays.

grammar.title: Comparing with 比
grammar.body: A 比 B + adjective: 北京比丹麦热. Add 多了 for 'much more' or 一点 for 'a bit'. Don't use 很 in a 比 sentence.

grammar.title: A 跟 B (不)一样
grammar.body: A 跟 B 一样 = A is the same as B; 不一样 = different. You can add an adjective: 跟…一样好.

grammar.title: 虽然…但是… / 因为…所以…
grammar.body: Chinese uses both halves of these pairs: 虽然有点辣，但是很好吃 (although…, (but)…), 因为…，所以… (because…, (so)…). In casual speech one half is often dropped.

dialogue.title: Listening challenge: Questions from her aunt
dialogue.setting: At a big family dinner in Beijing, her aunt has lots of questions. Natural speed. Try it without the text first.

questions.q: Has 米格 been to China before?
options: Yes, he used to live there

questions.q: What does he say about Chinese food?
options: It's the same as Danish food
It's different, a bit spicy, but delicious

questions.q: What does the aunt say about Beijing summers?
Why is 米格 learning Chinese?
options: To talk with his girlfriend's family
